title: Fibrant-replacement path model recognizes homotopy-cartesian squares
statement: Use small simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the functorial Kan--Quillen model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. For a commutative square with maps $a:Q\to X$, $b:Q\to Y$, $f:X\to Z$, $g:Y\to Z$ and $fa=gb$, call it homotopy cartesian when there exist factorizations $X\xrightarrow{i}X_f\xrightarrow{f_f}Z$ and $Y\xrightarrow{j}Y_f\xrightarrow{g_f}Z$ with $i,j$ weak equivalences and $f_f,g_f$ Kan fibrations such that the induced map $Q\to X_f\times_ZY_f$ is a weak equivalence. Let $r:\mathrm{id}\to R$ be any functorial fibrant replacement obtained by factoring each map to $\Delta^0$ into a trivial cofibration followed by a Kan fibration. Put $$P_R=RX\times_{RZ,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,RZ)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,RZ}RY.$$ Then the original square is homotopy cartesian if and only if the map $RQ\to P_R$ with coordinates $Ra,Rb$ and the constant path at $(Rf)(Ra)=(Rg)(Rb)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No Kan or nonemptiness assumption on $Q,X,Y,Z$ is imposed.

source.place: Paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient adjunction, through the sharp-map calculus: agent-explicit comparison between Rezk Section 2.3 (printed p.4) and the functorial Kan-replacement path model, using the existing constant-path comparison and strict-pullback invariance nodes. Rezk paper read online at https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/rezk-sharp-maps.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Write $A=RX$, $B=RY$, $C=RZ$, $D=RQ$, $F=Rf$ and $G=Rg$. The maps $r_T:T\to RT$ are weak equivalences and $RT$ is Kan. Use the model factorization axiom to choose $A\xrightarrow{\alpha}U\xrightarrow{p}C$ and $B\xrightarrow{\beta}V\xrightarrow{q}C$, with $\alpha,\beta$ trivial cofibrations and $p,q$ fibrations. Then $U,V$ are Kan. Put $K=Z\times_CU$ and $L=Z\times_CV$, using $r_Z:Z\to C$. Their projections $k:K\to Z$ and $l:L\to Z$ are fibrations. Here and below the horn-lifting definition proves pullback stability by projecting a lifting problem to the original fibration, and composition stability by taking successive lifts. Right properness applied to $r_Z$ and $p,q$ gives weak equivalences $K\to U$ and $L\to V$. Naturality of $r$ defines maps $s_X=(f,\alpha r_X):X\to K$ and $s_Y=(g,\beta r_Y):Y\to L$. Their composites to $U,V$ are weak equivalences, so two-out-of-three makes $s_X,s_Y$ weak equivalences. Thus these are admissible two-leg replacements of the original cospan.

proof.text: For any other admissible replacements $X\xrightarrow{i}X_f\to Z$ and $Y\xrightarrow{j}Y_f\to Z$, factor $f$ as a trivial cofibration $t:X\to T$ followed by a fibration $T\to Z$. The model lifting axiom applied to $t$ against $X_f\to Z$ and against $k$ gives maps $T\to X_f$ and $T\to K$ over $Z$ whose restrictions to $X$ are $i$ and $s_X$. Both maps are weak equivalences by two-out-of-three. Similarly obtain a fibration $S\to Z$, a trivial cofibration $Y\to S$, and weak equivalences $S\to Y_f$ and $S\to L$ under $Y$ over $Z$. Strict-pullback invariance now gives weak equivalences $T\times_Z S\to X_f\times_ZY_f$ and $T\times_Z S\to K\times_Z L$: in each application the base map is $1_Z$, both legs into $Z$ on the $T$ side of the cospans are fibrations, and both outer component maps are weak equivalences. The maps from $Q$ to these three pullbacks commute because the lifts restrict to the specified maps from $X,Y$. Two-out-of-three therefore shows that $Q\to X_f\times_ZY_f$ is a weak equivalence exactly when $c_0:Q\to K\times_Z L$ is. Since the replacements of step 1 exist, the definition's existential condition is equivalent to $c_0$ being a weak equivalence.

proof.text: Put $H=U\times_CV$. Apply strict-pullback invariance to the map of cospans $(K\to Z\leftarrow L)\to(U\to C\leftarrow V)$. The three component maps are weak equivalences by step 1, and the left legs $k,p$ are fibrations. Thus the coordinate map $w:K\times_ZL\to H$ is a weak equivalence. Define $d:D\to H$ by $(\alpha Ra,\beta Rb)$; its coordinates have the same image in $C$ since $F Ra=G Rb$. Naturality gives the exact equality $w c_0=d r_Q$. Since $w$ and $r_Q$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three shows that $c_0$ is a weak equivalence if and only if $d$ is.

proof.text: Let $E=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ with endpoint maps $e_0,e_1$. Apply the internal-Hom fibration-corner theorem to $\partial\Delta^1=\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and the Kan fibration $C\to\Delta^0$. Its target identifies degreewise with $C\times C$, so $(e_0,e_1):E\to C\times C$ is a Kan fibration. Define $E_B=E\times_{e_1,C,G}B$ and $E_V=E\times_{e_1,C,q}V$. The maps $E_B\to C\times B$ and $E_V\to C\times V$, given by $e_0$ and the other coordinate, are pullbacks of $(e_0,e_1)$ and hence fibrations. Their composites to $C$ are fibrations because $B,V$ are Kan: $C\times B\to C$ and $C\times V\to C$ are pullbacks of their terminal fibrations. Also $e_1:E\to C$ is a fibration, by composing $(e_0,e_1)$ with the projection whose other factor is the Kan complex $C$. Thus $E_V\to V$ is a fibration.

proof.text: The map $E_B\to E_V$ sends $(\gamma,b)$ to $(\gamma,\beta b)$. It is the pullback of the weak equivalence $\beta:B\to V$ along the fibration $E_V\to V$, since $q\beta=G$. Right properness makes it a weak equivalence. Apply strict-pullback invariance to $(E_B\xrightarrow{e_0}C\xleftarrow{F}A)\to(E_V\xrightarrow{e_0}C\xleftarrow{p}U)$, with component maps $E_B\to E_V$, $1_C$, and $\alpha$. The left legs are fibrations by step 4. After exchanging the two pullback coordinates this gives a weak equivalence $\phi:P_R=A\times_C E_B\to U\times_C E_V=P(p,q)$, explicitly $(a,\gamma,b)\mapsto(\alpha a,\gamma,\beta b)$.

proof.text: All of $U,V,C$ are Kan and $p,q$ are fibrations. The constant-path comparison theorem therefore gives a weak equivalence $\psi:H\to P(p,q)$, inserting the constant path at $p(u)=q(v)$. Let $c:D\to P_R$ be the map in the statement. The internal functor and constant-diagram definitions give the strict equality $\phi c=\psi d$: both sides have coordinates $\alpha Ra,\beta Rb$, and the constant path at $F Ra=G Rb$. Since $\phi,\psi$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three gives $c\in W$ if and only if $d\in W$. Steps 2 and 3 identify this condition with the original square being homotopy cartesian. Every construction used terminal fibrations, factorizations, lifts and degreewise pullbacks; it required neither an initial Kan hypothesis nor a chosen point. Thus the argument also includes empty simplicial sets.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q133-c1be1ad36 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all six steps and the full statements of the five cited nodes. The statement is true and not weakened. Rezk's existential two-leg definition holds iff Q→K×_Z L is a weak equivalence, iff RQ→U×_C V is one, iff RQ→P_R is one. I checked the edge cases Z empty (it forces RZ, RQ and P_R empty) and X empty with Z nonempty, and no step picks a point. Step 1: K→U is the pullback of r_Z along the fibration p, so right properness applies, and s_X is well defined by naturality (pα r_X = r_Z f). Step 2: lifts along trivial cofibrations against X_f→Z and k. The strict-pullback invariance node's hypotheses hold, with fibration legs T→Z, X_f→Z and k, and all components weak equivalences. The maps from Q commute. Step 3: w c_0 = d r_Q holds exactly. Step 4: the Mathlib leaf SSet.fibration_pullbackObjObjπ (PushoutProduct.lean:70-93) applied to ∂Δ¹↪Δ¹ and C→Δ⁰ makes (e0,e1) a fibration; E_B→C and E_V→V are fibrations as pullbacks and composites. Step 5: E_V×_V B = E_B, so right properness gives a weak equivalence, and the invariance node gives φ:P_R→P(p,q) with the right endpoint orientation. Step 6: the path-comparison node's Kan and fibration hypotheses hold, and φc = ψd holds strictly. There is no cycle over the 72 nodes the item reaches; the invariance and fibration-criterion nodes, which depend on the item, are not cited. Route: three cited nodes are in the same unit, plus one definition and one Mathlib leaf. No duplicate: lem-coef-kan-nerve-pullback-recognition needs Kan corners and uses ∞-cartesianness. No new nodes, no SGA, ten search records of all three kinds. Rezk and Kerodon are not in the literature folder; the report lists them as WANTED and proof_origin is agent. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem kan_fibrant_path_recognition {Q X Y Z : SSet.{u}} (a : Q ⟶ X) (b : Q ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : a ≫ f = b ≫ g) (R : SSet.{u} ⥤ SSet.{u}) (r : 𝟭 SSet.{u} ⟶ R) (hr : ∀ T : SSet.{u}, Mono (r.app T) ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (r.app T)) (hR : ∀ T : SSet.{u}, Fibration (stdSimplex.isTerminalObj₀.from (R.obj T))) : (∃ (Xf Yf : SSet.{u}) (i : X ⟶ Xf) (j : Y ⟶ Yf) (ff : Xf ⟶ Z) (gf : Yf ⟶ Z), i ≫ ff = f ∧ j ≫ gf = g ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence i ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence j ∧ Fibration ff ∧ Fibration gf ∧ ∃ c : Q ⟶ pullback ff gf, c ≫ pullback.fst ff gf = a ≫ i ∧ c ≫ pullback.snd ff gf = b ≫ j ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence c) ↔ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (homotopyPullbackComparison (R.map a) (R.map b) (R.map f) (R.map g) ((R.map_comp a f).symm.trans ((congrArg R.map h).trans (R.map_comp b g))))
